headline: Mmamapudi Kubjane wins 2026 Stephen Lawn TB-HIV Research Leadership Prize
dek: The South African epidemiologist and modeller was recognised for TB and HIV research that has helped shape South Africa's national TB strategy, the LSHTM Tuberculosis Centre said.
body:
Dr Mmamapudi Kubjane has been named recipient of the 2026 Stephen Lawn TB-HIV Research Leadership Prize, the LSHTM Tuberculosis Centre announced on LinkedIn.

Dr Kubjane is a South African epidemiologist and mathematical modeller at the Health Economics and Epidemiology Research Office. According to the post, she was recognised for her outstanding contributions to TB and HIV research, including work that has helped shape South Africa's national TB strategy and inform decisions on prevention, diagnosis and treatment.

The prize was presented by Professor Toyin Togun, Co-Director of the LSHTM Tuberculosis Centre, at the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (The Union) World Conference on Lung Health in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

The Stephen Lawn Prize is a collaboration between the TB Centre at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, the Desmond Tutu Health Foundation and The Union, with support from The Lancet Group. The centre said the award celebrates emerging research leaders whose work is helping advance TB and HIV research in sub-Saharan Africa.
